summary: קָטֹן describes something as small in relation to another. Genesis 1:16 uses it to distinguish the lesser of the two great lights. In Genesis 9:24 it identifies Noah’s youngest son.

senses.definition: Small in comparison with another of the same kind.

evidence.note: Of the two great lights, the one governing the day is called הַגָּדֹל and the one governing the night הַקָּטֹן.

senses.definition: Younger or youngest in relation to others in a family or group.

evidence.note: The phrase בְּנוֹ הַקָּטָן singles out Noah’s youngest son by his age among his brothers.

opposites.note: The same noun הַמָּאוֹר introduces each light, with גָּדוֹל and קָטֹן distinguishing the two.
